# Linus Torvalds "Did What I Preach", Used AI To Make Code Decipherable & Uncovered More Bugs

> "Nils Ollrogge reported a bug in the assoc_array library and had a patch to fix it too, but that code was too obscure for me to follow, so I did what I preach: use modern LLM tools to help make sense of it all. So this is an LLM-assisted branch which makes the code more readable by splitting up some of the larger and hard-to-read functions. The code was then run through a test harness in user space, which not only confirmed the bug Nils reported, but found three other bugs too - all going back to the very first commit adding this library back in 2013."

# Linux 7.3-rc6 Released: Normal For The New "AI Normal"

> "Nothing looks strange this week - unlike last week's slightly unusual diffstat, we're back to the normal "half the diff is driver fixes" so we're back to normality. The driver side is all over: gpu, networking, usb, tty, iio, sound... A little bit of everything, in other words. The commit counts are also normal (for the new "AI normal" with a lot of small error path handling fixes etc). Aside from the driver side, the usual suspects show up: architecture updates (mostly kvm-related again), core networking, some filesystem work (mainly smb client this time), bpf... And a number of new selftests too. Next week might look a bit different: we've got the annual maintainer summit and the Linux plumbers conference going on , so I'll be on the road, as will a number of other maintainers. That may or may not end up changing the stats for -rc7. But it's unlikely to affect the release schedule, although the fact that I have my yearly family vacation the week after that might make the next merge window a bit wonky. We will see."
